subject: Suppressing ticks on x axis only; space between y axis and label

messages.author: daf1376694d3d928
messages.subject: Suppressing ticks on x axis only; space between y axis and label
parts:
Hi,

I'm plotting several clusters of bars, with only one x value per
cluster, so I'd like to try to suppress the single tick mark at the
bottom of each cluster. Table 8.1 in the ggplot2 book mentions
'axis.ticks' and 'axis.ticks.y', so I tried 'axis.ticks.x', eventually
discovering this option was removed:

http://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/commit/1fb07117af63fa0e9ab49b2f7eae0363d3a9fad5

Is there another method of affecting the x axis ticks without the y
axis ones?

In the same plot, I have a log2-scale y axis with an axis label. Is it
possible to increase the space (which currently appears to be zero)
between the tick labels and axis label?

Thanks.

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Suppressing ticks on x axis only; space between y axis and label
parts:
Hi Nicholas,

I'd just set the breaks on the x axis to NA - e.g.

qplot(mpg, wt, data = mtcars) + scale_x_continuous(breaks = NA)
qplot(factor(cyl), wt, data = mtcars) + scale_x_discrete(breaks = NA)

Regards,

Hadley

PS. I've corrected that table in the book to avoid future confusion.

This is a poor spacing choice which I hope to improve in the next
version. In the meantime, the easiest solution is probably just to
add a new line to the axis label:

scale_y_log2('Speedup (1.0 = CPython 2.4.1)\n')

Hadley

messages.author: a9a25e4e3ab491e8
messages.subject: problems with scale_y_logit, custom transforms
parts:
Hadley and folks--

I'd like to be able to use scale_y_logit() and
coord_trans(ytrans="invlogit") to construct a plot summarizing some
proportion data. I have two problems:

1) scale_y_logit() fails with the error

Error in plogis(q, location, scale, lower.tail, log.p) : Non-numeric
argument to mathematical function

You can see this with the following code:

--8<---------------cut here---------------start------------->8---
library(boot) # logit()
library(ggplot2)

## load binomial data, compute proportion (disregarding sample size
## for this example)
data(cbpp, package="lme4")
cbpp <- within(cbpp, prop <- incidence/size)

## plot the mean proportion. works.
ggplot(cbpp, aes(x=as.numeric(period), y=prop)) +
stat_summary(fun.y=mean, geom="line")

## plot the logit of the mean proportion by hand. works.
ggplot(cbpp, aes(x=as.numeric(period), y=prop)) +
stat_summary(fun.y=function(y) logit(mean(y)), geom="line")

## use a transformer to get the logit of the mean proportion.
## breaks with error reported above
ggplot(cbpp, aes(x=as.numeric(period), y=prop)) +
stat_summary(fun.y=mean, geom="line") +
scale_y_logit()
--8<---------------cut here---------------end--------------->8---

Also, maybe I've got things backwards here, but why does the transformer
to put things onto the logit scale call plogis? plogis takes values in
the logit space and returns probabilities. qlogis takes probabilities
and returns results in logit space.

qlogis(0) # -Inf, logit space
plogis(0) # 0.5, probability space

For a transformation from probability space into logit space, which is
what I think scale_y_logit() is supposed to do, don't we want qlogis?

2) invlogit isn't defined as a possible transform

At the end of the above plot, I'd ideally like to add something like

+ coord_trans(ytrans="invlogit") # should use plogis?

But that transformer is not in the list in table 6.2 of the book. So,
is it possible to define new transformers? What do they have to look
like?

Thanks for any help,
/au

--
Austin Frank
http://aufrank.net
GPG Public Key (D7398C2F): http://aufrank.net/personal.asc

Yes, you're right. Fixed in the development version too.

> For a transformation from probability space into logit space, which is
> what I think scale_y_logit() is supposed to do, don't we want qlogis?
>
> 2) invlogit isn't defined as a possible transform
>
> At the end of the above plot, I'd ideally like to add something like
>
>  + coord_trans(ytrans="invlogit") # should use plogis?

To define your own transformer, call Trans$new. It takes three
arguments: the function, it's inverse, and a function to create
labels. A few examples should give you the idea:

TransLog2 <- Trans$new("log2", "log2", function(x) 2^x, function(x)
bquote(2^.(x)))
TransPow10 <- Trans$new("pow10",function(x) 10^x, "log10", function(x) log10(x))

Does that help?

Hadley
